articles.title: Fermin Lopez snubs Manchester United interest as Barcelona star pledges long-term future to Camp Nou
articles.summary: Barcelona starlet Fermin Lopez has handed Manchester United a significant blow by publicly rejecting their advances in favour of a long-term stay at Camp Nou...
articles.body:
Barcelona starlet Fermin Lopez has handed Manchester United a significant blow by publicly rejecting their advances in favour of a long-term stay at Camp Nou. The 23-year-old midfielder has emerged as a top target for the Premier League giants following a string of sensational performances in La Liga.

Man Utd have stepped up their search for midfield reinforcements, and Fermin has reportedly climbed to the top of their wishlist. The Red Devils have long been admirers of the Spanish international, whose versatility and goal-scoring threat from midfield have made him one of the most exciting young talents in European football. With the Premier League side looking to rebuild their squad, they had identified the La Masia graduate as a primary objective for upcoming transfer windows.

However, the English giants face a monumental task in pryign the player away from Catalonia. Despite the allure of Old Trafford and the financial might of the Premier League, Fermin has shown no desire to entertain a move abroad. His profile has only grown after a dominant display against Alaves , where he proved once again why he is considered indispensable to the sporting project currently being spearheaded by the Catalan club.

Addressing the speculation surrounding a potential move to the Premier League, Fermin was quick to shut down any talk of an exit. Speaking in the aftermath of his MVP-winning performance, the midfielder made it clear that his heart belongs to the Blaugrana. The player's definitive stance will likely force Man Utd to look elsewhere as they seek to bolster their options in the middle of the park.

"I don't pay attention to this type of news. I want to be at Barca as long as possible and I hope to finish my career at this club," he stated frmly, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo .

The transfer speculation comes in the wake of a truly dominant individual display by Fermin during Barcelona's demolition of Alaves. The 23-year-old was the architect of the victory, producing a stunning goal and providing two assists for Raphinha to secure the three points. His influence on the pitch was so profound that he was comfortably named the Man of the Match, further justifying Hansi Flick's faith in his abilities.

Reflecting on the team's performance, the midfielder suggested that the squad had successfully navigated a difficult period to find their best form again. "We have made a good match, we have found ourselves again, we managed to recover our identity and our true level and now we must continue playing in this way," he explained.

Flick's tactical demands and squad fatigue

Despite his starring role, Fermin admitted that the intensity of Flick's system is beginning to take its toll physically. During the latter stages of the Alaves encounter, the midfielder was visibly exhausted, yet he was asked to push through the fatigue to maintain the team's structural integrity. This high-octane approach has become a hallmark of Barcelona's play this season, demanding maximum effort from every player on the pitch for the full 90 minutes.

Revealing a touchline conversation with his manager, Fermin shared the instructions he received while struggling for breath. "Flick told me, although he knew I was dead, that he was going to change De Jong and for me to hold on a bit and be calmer," he revealed.

articles.title: Biggest issue from Oklahoma's 42-25 loss to South Carolina
articles.summary: The big problem that Oklahoma's embarrassing blowout loss to South Carolina exposed.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners fell to 4-4 overall and 2-3 in SEC play on Saturday afternoon at home, losing by a final score of 42-25 against the South Carolina Gamecocks . Head coach Brent Venables' team was thoroughly embarrassed on their home field in Norman.

OU was completely outclassed and out-coached by the Gamecocks, once again failing to build on the previous week's success. Again, the Sooners were more short-handed due to injuries, less disciplined, and not as hungry as their opponent. This has been happening at an alarming rate over the last few seasons.

There is plenty to discuss after this game, including how OU's normally strong defense completely fell apart against South Carolina. Of course, the OU offense offered no help whatsoever. It was ultimately rinse and repeat for the Sooners. Show a sign of life one week, and then completely fall flat on your face the next.

So with that being said, here is the biggest issue from OU's loss at the hands of head coach Shane Beamer and the Gamecocks.

Oklahoma is failing to meet the standard

Oklahoma Football is one of the five greatest programs in the history of college football. The blue-blooded Sooners have built a longtime tradition of winning championships at the highest level, led by legendary coaches like Bud Wilkinson, Barry Switzer, and Bob Stoops. However, OU is nowhere near meeting the standard the program has set.

Saturday's loss ensured the Sooners won't accomplish anything of note in four of Venables' five seasons at the helm. Aside from a magical November 2025 that led OU to the College Football Playoff, Venables has simply not been good enough at OU.

With four games left in the year, Oklahoma will have to win at least two games to reach six wins and a bowl game, and that's no guarantee. Even then, it would tie the worst regular-season record OU has had since 1999, and all three seasons have come under the current regime. For Venables, the majority of the time he's been in charge in Norman, the Sooners have been a .500 program.

South Carolina offensive coordinator Kendal Briles ran circles around Venables on Saturday. It was a startling scene for an OU defense that usually keeps the Sooners in games while the offense falters. Of course, the offense played true to form and faltered at every opportunity, as offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle was completely overmatched against South Carolina defensive coordinator Clayton White.

Arbuckle is clearly in over his head in the SEC, and it's hard to understand how Venables hasn't seen enough to send him packing yet. Unlike his head coach, Arbuckle doesn't have a massive buyout, because he wasn't given a contract extension before this season began. He was putting up big numbers at Washington State, but the young play-caller is painfully out of his depth against the big boys.

As Oklahoma continues to stumble through a 2026 season that had so much promise in the preseason, it's becoming increasingly clear that Venables will have to completely clean house on offense. It's really the only choice he has if he wants to save his own job. Everything else to fix the offense has already been tried. The players and coaches on that side of the ball aren't getting the job done.

Venables' hefty buyout and the optics of firing him after extending his contract will keep him safe this year, but his days at OU are clearly numbered if things don't change.

Oklahoma's standard is so much higher than what is happening on the field right now. When teams like South Carolina come into Norman, the Sooners are supposed to dominate the game from start to finish and walk out with an easy win. Instead, the script was flipped. OU is supposed to win national championships, not be an also-ran in the SEC two-thirds of the time.

Wearing that logo means something. When you wear it, you represent a fanbase so passionate about the Sooners, and your job is to uphold the tradition of winning that came before you. That's not happening right now, and it hasn't happened with consistency in years.

What happens between now and next season, and ultimately what happens over the next few years, will determine whether the people working for Oklahoma want things to change, or if they're fine coasting on what OU once was.

The people running the show in Norman haven't been good enough, and Oklahoma has to get back to being Oklahoma. That means winning at the highest level, and doing that with extreme consistency. OU loves touting its blue-blood status, but ultimately, you have to operate at a blue-blood level to keep it.

articles.title: Commanders' bad luck continues
articles.summary: It seems like the Commanders just can't catch a break.
articles.body:
"If it wasn't for bad luck, I wouldn't have no luck at all." How many times have you heard that statement over the years? That saying sort of fits the Washington Commanders .

On Friday, 11 days after seeing star wide receiver Terry McLaurin tear his patellar tendon and be lost for the season, defensive tackle Daron Payne fractured his foot in Friday's practice, also knocking him out for the season. Payne, Washington's 2018 first-round pick, had been considered a potential trade candidate ahead of the November 10 NFL trade deadline.

Now, Washington's best trade chip isn't going anywhere. At 1-4-1, the Commanders are in a weird position. While some consider them already out of contention, they play in the suddenly weak NFC East and trail the New York Giants by only three games. General manager Adam Peters may have surveyed the NFC East landscape and thought the same thing. Why trade Payne if the Commanders remain in the NFC playoff race?

Here's where we come back to Washington's bad luck. Now, Peters doesn't even have a decision to make. The Commanders aren't getting a draft pick for Payne if they keep losing. Nor will they have him on the field, potentially helping them string together several wins and get back into the playoff hunt.

One day after Payne injured his foot, Mike Florio of NBC Sports' Pro Football Talk said that the Commanders were talking to multiple teams about Payne.

The Commanders, we're told, were talking to one or more teams about the terms of a potential trade for veteran defensive tackle Daron Payne. After he suffered a season-ending foot injury during practice on Friday, there will be no trade.

Washington was talking to multiple teams. Do you know what that means? When you have more than one team bidding for a player, the better the compensation you receive. We'll never know now.

The Commanders just can't catch a break.

articles.title: Cardiff warned of complacency amid winless away form
articles.summary: Only strugglers Preston and Watford have fewer points than Cardiff City on the road in the Championship this season.
articles.body:
Cardiff City cannot get complacent in their bid to find comfort in the Championship, and have been warned they could be in for a shock if they do.

Promoted from League One, the Bluebirds have not looked out of place in their first season back in the second tier.

They have caught the eye with their brand of football, sticking to the style that brought them success with a young side last term, and have not been without some impressive results.

But they have also not been able to drag themselves away from the bottom end of the table, with Saturday's 3-0 defeat at Wolves keeping Brian Barry-Murphy's side in 18th.

"It was an all-round lacklustre performance," said former Cardiff and Wales striker Nathan Blake after the beating at Molineux, the Bluebirds' first in four games.

"You could say they had one or two opportunities in the second half, but Cardiff didn't deserve anything from the game.

"The performance level was poor. Wolves didn't get out of second gear."

Defeat in the Black Country left Cardiff with just two points from seven games on the road this season. Only Watford and Preston have returned fewer.

"They will have to turn it around pretty quickly because the pressure will come at home," Blake added to BBC Radio Wales Sport.

"If they're drawing or don't pick up wins, then all of a sudden you're back in a relegation battle.

"I don't think it will happen – they play too good [a brand of] football – but I don't want to be complacent and say it won't happen."

Just to underline the point, Cardiff have fewer points (14) than they did after 13 games when they were relegated from the Championship two terms ago (15).

And yet, that seems out of keeping with a side that has convinced many they should not really be looking over their shoulders.

Their form at Cardiff City Stadium, where they have won the past three outings, is doing some heavy lifting.

"They play such good football that often the performance is what you're left with in terms of positivity. Sooner or later they'll give somebody a hiding or go on a run," said Blake.

"The manager will have to really gee the players up for the next game because those sort of performances weren't acceptable.

"Playing like that, you're not going to come home with many points."

Fortunately, Cardiff's next two fixtures before the international break are at Cardiff City Stadium, with West Ham to come on Wednesday, 4 November (19:45 GMT) before they host strugglers Burnley.

Whoever the opponent, the Bluebirds still have work to do in both boxes before anyone can relax.

Cardiff's issues at the back were exposed early at Molineux, as they shipped two goals within 15 minutes, with Wolves hardly breaking a sweat.

The visitors had – and continue to have – genuine injury issues at the back, which Barry-Murphy loathed to criticise too harshly, but even he knew it was not good enough.

"All three goals from our point of view were very disappointing and very soft," he said.

"We came here – despite Wolves' reputation and where they've come from – to win the game, but we defended the box really poorly in those situations.

"If you give teams like this the ball in the areas we did, then you are vulnerable.

"It's an insight for us what we have to do against teams of this calibre to give ourselves a chance to win the game."

They should not need a 3-0 beating to be aware of such simple things as tracking runners, but it is worth noting there were two divisions between the sides last season.

And – according to the statistics at least – Barry-Murphy's charges gave as good as they got.

As they have done in many games this season, they bossed possession and got shots away.

In fact, Cardiff had more shots on target (nine) than their three-goal hosts (four) and - based on xG - deserved at least one goal to have made the contest interesting.

But then, Cardiff are not afraid of shooting. Only Middlesbrough and West Ham have had more shots this season.

Barry-Murphy suggested his side should have worked Wolves goalkeeper Jose Sa more often, but Blake was less than convinced by a game already lost by defensive frailties.

"Wolves were only five or six out of ten, they weren't brilliant," said Blake, a man who won promotion to the Premier League in Old Gold.

"They just weren't challenged to step up a gear, so you don't know if they had another level in the bag. The goals were just too easy.

" Cardiff had a massive contingent of away fans, but it was probably the quietest I've ever heard two and a half thousand fans in my life.

"They were waiting for the team to give them something - but through the 90 minutes Cardiff didn't deliver."

Cardiff will have the chance again on Wednesday as they look to find a bit more home comfort in the Championship before any concern starts to grow.

articles.title: Barcelona reach unprecedented goal difference milestone after 11 La Liga games
articles.summary: Barcelona’s start to the new season has been stellar, and barring the two defeats to PSG and Real Madrid which came as a shock, they have been simply unstopp...
articles.body:
Barcelona's start to the new season has been stellar, and barring the two defeats to PSG and Real Madrid which came as a shock, they have been simply unstoppable.

Beyond just stringing wins together for fun, it is the manner in which Hansi Flick's side have done the same that has caught the attention of the world.

After all, the rate at which they have been scoring goals has been exceptional, and they have almost made it a norm to score four to five goals in every outing.

One of Barcelona's many goalscoring machines. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

At this point, Barcelona have played eleven games in La Liga and have scored a stunning 46 goals in that duration with an average of over four goals per game.

Overall, they have conceded 12 goals in the same timeframe, and their goal difference thus stands at a staggering +34.

That number, quite unanimously, is considered the largest in La Liga history after eleven match days. While there may not be any accurate records of the early years, such a massive difference at such an early stage in the season is almost unheard of.

Barcelona put six goals past Alaves. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Barcelona's 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid last weekend was a rare anomaly in the team's calendar, for they have scored in abundance in almost every other game in La Liga.

Many expected the team's momentum to take a blow after suffering two back-to-back defeats, especially given how they struck where it hurts most.

Yet, Flick's men seem to have comfortably moved past the slump. They got back to winning ways last night against Deportivo Alaves , and did it in their traditional dominant style as they scored six goals against the visitors.

Raphinha and Lamine Yamal netted braces, while Anthony Gordon and Fermin Lopez scored the other goals for the team on the night. With the players once again picking up form, the goal difference could go on increasing with every passing game.

Given that the next league clash is against Atletico Madrid, Barcelona will be determined to take a win away from the Riyadh Air Metropolitano, and thereby make a statement to the world once again.

The Washington Commanders are already down one receiving option as Terry McLaurin is on injured reserve. Treylon Burks stepped up admirably in last Monday's loss to the San Francisco 49ers , catching four passes for 66 yards but suffered an injury to his foot along the way.

Burks, in his fifth year out of Arkansas, is on track to have his most productive campaign since his rookie year. He was downgraded to questionable on the injury report for Sunday night's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Here's what we know about his chances of suiting up in the Week 8 clash of NFC East rivals.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, Burks is expected to lace them up and participate against the Eagles. The update came alongside other news about wide receivers dealing with injuries (for reference George Pickens is expected to play and Jaylen Waddle is trending in the right direction).

With McLaurin out there is no sure-thing No. 1 receiver for Jayden Daniels to lock onto. Burks has to be considered a decent option among the group of Chig Okonkwo and Antonio Williams. All three saw their roles increase against San Francisco.

There's really no telling what type of effort the Eagles are going to put forward with their backs against the wall and without Jalen Hurts. Their defense is coming off an uninspired showing in a 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football .

While there's always some risk involved dialing up a fringe option, Burks would be a decent play for that last wide receiver spot or flex position for teams that do not have more appealing options. These two teams tend to play entertaining, competitive games even when the rosters aren't of the same quality so rooting for a shootout is one route to fantasy victory.

articles.standfirst: Tiene muchas variantes para formar la defensa frente al Aston Villa
articles.summary: Tiene muchas variantes para formar la defensa frente al Aston Villa
articles.body: El Barcelona juega este martes un partido clave de cara a su clasificación en la liguilla de la Champions frente al Aston Villa. No será, ni mucho menos, una tarea fácil. El equipo de Emery ha ganado los tres partidos disputados en esta competición y lidera la tabla junto a otros equipos. Además de la dificultad que representa la calidad del rival, el conjunto azulgrana llega muy mermado en cuanto a efectivos en defensa. Esta circunstancia provoca un mar de dudas en Hansi Flick, que no tiene muy claro cuál es la mejor opción para este partido teniendo en cuenta las bajas. Frente al Alavés, el alemán hizo pruebas. Situó a Brian Fariñas en el lateral derecho y a Frenkie de Jong como central. Ambos respondieron satisfactoriamente. La duda reside en si pueden ofrecer ese mismo nivel frente a un equipo tan potente como el Aston Villa. Y eso no está nada claro. Flick tiene más alternativas. Andreas Christensen se entrenó este domingo con el resto de sus compañeros después de un mes de baja por lesión. Parece muy precipitado que Flick lo alinee como titular frente a los ingleses. En primer lugar, por el poco tiempo que ha entrenado con sus compañeros. Por otra parte, y más importante, porque es un futbolista muy propenso a las lesiones y las recaídas. El riesgo es muy grande. Si el entrenador no quiere apostar por De Jong, lo lógico sería que Gerard Martín, que es el titular pero que falló ante el Madrid, formara pareja con Cubarsí en el centro de la zaga. Tanto Koundé como Eric García están descartados para el choque porque siguen lesionados. Las dudas también están en los laterales. La lógica invita a pensar que Flick alineará a Cancelo y Balde, a pesar de que no está nada contento con este último. La opción de apostar por Fariñas parece muy arriesgada. No es lo mismo enfrentarse al Alavés que al Aston Villa, sobre todo teniendo en cuenta que el partido del pasado sábado fue su debut con el primer equipo. Si el técnico tiene muchas dudas en defensa, en el resto del equipo, en cambio, todo parece bastante claro. Rodri y Pedri formarán juntos el doble pivote; la línea de tres la integrarán Lamine Yamal, Fermín y Gordon (Adeyemi no aprovechó la oportunidad frente al Alavés); y Raphinha ocupará la punta de ataque.

articles.title: WSL round-up: Alessia Russo scores late equaliser to salvage draw for Arsenal as Man City hold on to beat London City
articles.summary: Sky Sports' round-up of Sunday's WSL action as Arsenal are held to a frustrating 1-1 draw with Aston Villa; Man City move top of the WSL table with an impressive 2-1 win away from home against London City Lionesses; Tottenham, West Ham and Brighton also won
articles.body:
Alessia Russo scored a late equaliser to salvage a 1-1 draw for Arsenal against Aston Villa as Renee Slegers' side failed to make their dominance count at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners had 27 shots in total at the Emirates but were left frustrated by a stoic defensive performance from Villa, who sat deep to preserve their lead after Chasity Grant scored with their only shot of the game in the 25th minute.

Villa defended valiantly, supported by eight saves from Akane Okuma, before Russo latched onto Stina Blackstenius' cross to head home the equaliser in the 85th minute.

Arsenal pushed for a late winner but ultimately left themselves with too much to do on an afternoon where their finishing left a lot to be desired.

Manchester City kept the pressure on Chelsea at the top of the table with a win against London City Lionesses 2-1 at Hayes Lane.

Mary Earps' brilliant double save kept the visitors out before the break, but Bunny Shaw rounded her to open the scoring with her ninth goal of the season soon after.

Jana Fernandez headed the hosts level from a set-piece, only for Lauren Hemp to restore City's lead just 122 seconds later, finishing from Mary Fowler's delivery. Shaw also hit the post, but two goals proved enough.

A frustrating afternoon for London City, a valuable three points for City.

Chelsea remain top of the WSL after an emphatic 6-0 win at Charlton, with Melvine Malard scoring twice in a ruthless first-half display.

Nathalie Bjorn headed the visitors ahead before Malard and Ellie Carpenter added to the lead.

Malard's second made it four before the break, while substitutes Aggie Beever-Jones and Giulia Dragoni joined the scoring in the second half. It was Dragoni's first Chelsea goal.

The only real concern for Chelsea was Lauren James, who had been causing plenty of problems before being forced off around the 30-minute mark.

Charlton kept searching for a consolation, but there was no reward on a bruising afternoon for the hosts.

Tottenham cruised to a 4-1 win away at Birmingham City thanks to a blistering second-half performance.

The hosts threatened in the early stages after Geum-Min Lee hit the bar but Julie Blakstad's opener swung momentum in Spurs favour.

Olivia Holdt's free-kick and Signe Gaupset's driven effort made it 3-0, with two goals scored in just three minutes.

Nebe Harron's flicked effort sparked faint hopes of a comeback but the win was sealed when Victoria Pelova made it four with just over five minutes to go.

West Ham dominated Liverpool as a double from Viviane Asseyi helped the Hammers secure a 4-1 win at home.

Asseyi's first arrived from the penalty spot in just the seventh minute before Leila Wandeler and Laia Codina also scored before the break.

A perfectly placed free-kick from Asseyi would make it four, with Viviene Endemann's late goal only a consolation in what was a difficult trip to the capital for the Reds.

Brighton finally made their pressure count as second-half goals from Caitlin Hayes and Sophie Peskett secured a 2-1 comeback win over Crystal Palace.

The hosts controlled much of the game but were left chasing it after Annabel Blanchard's stunning strike from outside the box gave Palace the lead.

Fran Kirby had earlier passed up a promising chance, while visiting goalkeeper Pauline Peyraud-Magnin kept Brighton frustrated.

Hayes eventually broke through, heading home Manuela Vanegas' cross, before Emilie Joramo picked out Peskett to slot in the winner.

Brighton saw out three minutes of added time to claim a deserved three points.

articles.title: Falkirk 2-0 Celtic: Martin O'Neill's Hoops denied chance to go seven points clear in Scottish Premiership by brilliant Bairns
articles.summary: Report as Falkirk stun Celtic with 2-0 win; Ethan Ross gifted the opener and Scott Tanser doubled the lead before half time; Jacob Murrell had a third ruled out for handball; Celtic remain four points clear of title rivals Rangers having played a game more; Falkirk are up to fourth
articles.body:
Martin O'Neill made three changes as he looked for a response after Celtic's midweek draw with Dundee United, but they were outclassed by the Bairns, who extended their winning run to four matches.

Ethan Ross was gifted the opening goal just three minutes into the game. Ryan Strain sent a cross into the box and Cameron Carter-Vickers sent the ball straight to him to fire into the net.

Scott Bain was more than impressive against his former team, denying Camilo Duran and Hasseim Hassan before Falkirk stunned with their second, this time Scott Tanser beating Carter-Vickers before lashing the ball into the net.

The hosts had the ball in the net again after the break, but it was ruled out with VAR confirming the ball came off Jacob Murrell's arm before crossing the line.

Celtic piled on the pressure late on, but could not find a way past Bain, who made 10 saves as Martin O'Neill's side endured an afternoon of frustration and suffered a sixth defeat in 10 matches.

They remain four points clear of title rivals Rangers having played a game more. Falkirk are up to fourth, two points behind Hearts.

The key moments from the Falkirk Stadium

3: GOAL FALKIRK! Ryan Strain sends a cross into the box, Cameron Carter-Vickers sends the ball straight to Ethan Ross instead of clearing the danger, and he makes no mistake.

12: OFF THE POST! Camilo Duran gets on the end of a long ball from Liam Scales, but his shot smacks off the post.

21: SAVE! Falkirk threaten again. Jacob Murrell surges into the box, his shot comes off Carter-Vickers and Sam Johnstone saves.

29: SAVE! Celtic should be level! Hasseim Hassan's cross is met by Duran and he heads it straight at Scott Bain to palm away.

33: SAVE! Duran denied by Bain again! Callum McGregor with a lovely ball through to the striker, the Falkirk keeper gets low to block his shot.

38: GOAL FALKIRK! Scott Tanser collects the ball and eases past Carter-Vickers before firing into the bottom corner.

44: SAVE! Duran is again denied by Bain before he pushes the resultant corner clear.

50: GOAL FALKIRK! Celtic fail to deal with a long throw, Johnstone sends the ball into the path of Murrell. It does appear to hit his hand before crossing the line.

52: NO GOAL! VAR confirms handball as Murrell's third is ruled out.

60: CHANCE! Falkirk try to clear from a corner, it falls to McGregor and he fails to find the target.

67: DOUBLE SAVE! Brilliant from Bain. He pushes James Forrest's strike clear, then recovers to deny Benjamin Nygren on the rebound.

76: OVER! What a chance for Scales. He scored Celtic's equaliser in midweek, but he heads over the bar.

81: SAVE! Nygren curls in a free-kick. Bain gets his hand to it, although it looked like it was over.

82: SAVE! What a game Bain is having against his former club. This time, he denies Baur.

Sky Sports' Chris Sutton was watching at the Falkirk Stadium:

"Celtic have had issues all season. It's not a great surprise that Celtic have come to Falkirk and been rolled over.

"They weren't great in the week, and I still don't think Martin O'Neill knows his best XI.

"There's not an area of the team or the club that is functioning as it should this season and that's a problem.

"There's this big debate about Shaun Maloney and Mark Fotheringham and their coaching, or is it on Martin?

"This is all on Martin because he employs the coaches and he will ask them to play and train in a certain way.

"It's hard to see how Celtic are actually set up. It's a bit off the cuff - get the ball to Hassan and hope he can do something.

"That's the way it has been essentially all season."

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill on Sky Sports:

"A tough one to take because I know we conceded two goals but we could have scored six or seven dead easily.

"Their goalkeeper was magnificent on the day - he made some remarkable saves - and we played some really decent stuff as well too on that surface.

"We're still top of the league. We came from a mile behind last year to win the league. A mile behind on two or three occasions as well.

"We're still in a decent position at this minute. We've played a lot of football as well.

"I keep out the noise at the end of it all. I've managed this team now for about a year, give or take a month or two, and I've managed before.

"Celtic are used to winning, as you can tell by the number of trophies they've won in the last 25 years."

Falkirk manager John McGlynn on Sky Sports:

"Huge, huge, huge team effort. The work the boys put in, the desire, the hunger. Running miles for each other, blocking things, defending corner kicks.

"Absolutely delighted for everyone involved. They put so much into that game.

"No different to any other game that we'll play against Celtic - we'll always have to defend.

"We'll always have to rely on the goalkeeper to have a good game. That happened and we're delighted.

"We're four on the bounce. Three clean sheets in the last game, the last three games.

"When you're at home, you've got your home crowd behind you, you bust their gut for them as well.

"The great camaraderie and team spirit that we've got is that we're finding a way to win."

articles.title: Everything Bill Belichick Said After UNC Nearly Upset No. 1 Miami, Watch Full Video Following Loss
articles.summary: North Carolina just missed the signature win of the Bill Belichick era with a 38-35 loss to No. 1 Miami on Saturday, and the legendary head coach said he was "proud" of the team's effort in defeat.
articles.body:
North Carolina just missed the signature win of the Bill Belichick era with a 38-35 loss to No. 1 Miami on Saturday, and the legendary head coach said he was "proud" of the team's effort in defeat.

"Really proud of our effort tonight, but unfortunately, came up a little bit short," he told reporters after the game, per Jack Morris of On3.com. "Disappointing. Miami's really good, really good on offense. They've got two great players and a lot of other good players. We obviously had a hard time handling, although I thought we actually defended them pretty well. But I mean, they made a couple of great plays that you don't see too many other people make.

"So they're very good, very good on offense, and one-score, back and forth game, and then they got the turnover, and then it became a two-score game, and we couldn't get the onside kicks, so that's pretty much the story of it. A lot of effort, a lot of toughness, a lot of mental toughness, a lot of competitiveness, and just disappointing to come up short here two weeks in a row."

Belichick also said quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. performed at a "solid" level (1:15 mark) and praised him for spreading the ball around to a number of receivers.

"Billy's job is to throw the ball to the guy that's open," he said (5:37 mark). "We don't throw the ball to one receiver. Sometimes on a screen pass we do, but we don't just go back and say, 'Oh, we're going to throw to this guy. We're going to throw it to that guy.' We run the pattern based on the coverage. We throw the ball to the guy that has the most opportunity to catch it based on the coverage and the read that he gets, and there are different reads on different plays. So that's what he's supposed to do. That's what he did do. That's what he should do."

Edwards went 28-of-34 for 341 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions in a brilliant individual performance that could raise some questions about Miami's secondary moving forward when it will likely face better competition in the College Football Playoff.

Nine different Tar Heels caught passes, including tight end Jelani Thurman.

Thurman finished with five catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns, continuing an impressive season.

"It's been good all year," Belichick said of the chemistry between Edwards and Thurman (6:34 mark). "It was good in the spring. It was good in TCU. It was good tonight. They've been productive all year. We had trouble covering it in practice. It's a problem there, too. So it's been like that all year."

North Carolina led by four points in the fourth quarter before it gave up a touchdown, lost a fumble and gave up another touchdown in the defining stretch of the game. Despite that sequence, it still recovered two onside kicks near the end of the fourth quarter before they were both overturned by penalty.

Were it not for the penalties, the Tar Heels would have had a chance to win the game at the end.

While it was a disappointing loss to North Carolina, it is 4-4 on the season and looks much better than it did during Belichick's first season with a 4-8 record. Its final four games are against unranked opponents, so it will look to build some late momentum after Saturday's near-miss.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Drew Spence 'very proud' to break appearance record
articles.summary: Tottenham midfielder Drew Spence says it is a "very proud moment" to become the Women's Super League's all-time appearance record holder.
articles.body:
Tottenham midfielder Drew Spence says it is a "very proud moment" to become the Women's Super League's all-time appearance record holder.

Spence, 34, started in Tottenham's WSL game against Birmingham City on Sunday, making her 217th appearance in the competition.

She overtook ex-Chelsea captain Millie Bright and could become the only outfield player at Tottenham to play 90 minutes in all of their WSL games this season.

"I've been around for a while! I'm incredibly proud to be able to do that and it's not just a proud moment for me, but also for my family," Spence told BBC Sport.

"It's [about] all the hard work that I put in throughout the years. When you're younger, you don't really think about these types of accolades.

"It was all about winning trophies. Now it's happened, it's such a massive part of my career and something that I can be proud of to look back on.

"I know the sacrifices - looking after yourself and making sure that you're available all the time. I know how hard it is to keep that motivation for so many seasons."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Spence has played her entire career in London, spending 14 years at Chelsea before making the move to Tottenham in 2022.

She progressed from Arsenal and Fulham's academies and swapped nationalities from England to Jamaica in 2021.

During her time at Chelsea she won five league titles and four FA Cup trophies as part of one of England's most successful squads.

"She was a great team-mate, such a sweet soul off the pitch, but when she got on it, she was an absolute warrior," Chelsea midfielder Erin Cuthbert said.

"Technically, she's got the brains and the skillset. She looked after me from the very beginning [although] she welcomed me to the club with a two-footed challenge!

"She certainly deserves all the plaudits. To have that longevity is something I look up to. Now, she's a leader at Spurs."

Spence was named Tottenham captain in the summer and has gone on to become a key figure under manager Martin Ho.

In her first season at the club she played 22 games, more than in any campaign at Chelsea, and she has played every minute so far in 2026-27.

"I feel like I'm probably in the best shape that I've ever been. I'm recovering quicker, I understand my body a lot more and the nutrition side of things has helped me," said Spence.

"It's understanding what is right for me to recover and just little things. We have all those luxuries now which is amazing for the younger players."

Despite her achievements, Spence admits there are "regrets" from earlier in her career, when she wished she had understood how to prepare her body better.

She believes that could have given her more consistency while at Chelsea but acknowledges it is a lesson that has helped her flourish at Tottenham.

"I think people around me know that I've always just tried to do the best I can," added Spence.

"I have a lot of regrets in my career, but I'm at a stage now where I'm trying to be as consistent with my performance as I can and to lead the team.

"If I was more structured or understood my body better, I could have done that earlier in my career and given myself a better chance in certain points.

"But that's all part of the journey, that's all part of growing, that's all learning experiences. It's regrets within myself. But when I look back, I'll still be proud."

Tottenham manager Ho says Spence has earned "huge respect" at the club for the way she has applied herself since joining.

"Her performances and her ability to adapt and change - physically, technically, tactically - she's taken huge steps," he said.

"She's given herself longevity and she needs a lot of praise for that. I have massive respect for Drew as a professional, and as a person for what she's done for the game."

Spence was part of the Jamaica squad in 2023 that wrote an open letter calling for "immediate and systematic change" within the Jamaica Football Federation (JFF).

She has pushed for improved conditions in women's football and Ho says the "adversity" she has overcome has shaped the player Spence is today.

"She's used all those experiences to put herself in the position she is and she's grown from them," added Ho.

"I think Drew can play for as long as she wants. She's sharp, she's fit, very intelligent, a wonderful player for us and a really key part of what we're trying to do."

Spence still believes there is more to come too and has no plans to retire any time soon.

"There's parts of my game that I feel like I still need to improve on and I want to give it everything that I've got until I can't go any longer," she said.

"It was always my biggest dream [to play football] so I want to do it for as long as I can and enjoy it whilst I still can."

articles.title: Celtic 'team in regression' under Martin O'Neill and manager to blame, says Chris Sutton
articles.summary: Celtic missed the chance to move seven points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership; it was Falkirk's first win against the Hoops since 2007; Martin O'Neill's side have won just three of their last 10 games in all competitions
articles.body:
Sky Sports' Chris Sutton did not hold back after his former club fell to a shock 2-0 defeat at Falkirk , insisting he is watching a "team in regression."

Ethan Ross' early goal was added to by Scott Tanser's excellent finish, as Celtic's defensive frailties were exposed once again.

The defeat leaves Celtic with a record of three wins from their past 10 outings as they failed to extend their four-point lead at the top of the table, with Besiktas next in the Europa League, where they have lost three of three.

"The club and the team are in regression. They're just not a good functioning team at this moment in time," the former Hoops striker said.

"Martin will say they're top of the league but in Europe, they're ahead of a team from an outpost in Azerbaijan or Armenia, but that's it. They've been woeful in Europe.

"Celtic fans, quite rightly, expect more.

"Celtic have had issues all season. It's not a great surprise that Celtic have come to Falkirk and been rolled over.

"They weren't great in the week and I still don't think Martin O'Neill knows his best XI.

"There's not an area of the team or the club that is functioning as it should this season and that's a problem.

"There's this big debate about Shaun Maloney and Mark Fotheringham and their coaching, or is it on Martin?

"This is all on Martin because he employs the coaches and he will ask them to play and train in a certain way.

"It's hard to see how Celtic are actually set up. It's a bit off the cuff - get the ball to Hassan and hope he can do something.

"That's the way it has been essentially all season."

The defeat was Celtic's second in the Premiership this season, and followed their 2-2 draw at home to Dundee United.

But for the manager, there is no reason to panic.

"We're still top of the league," O'Neill told Sky Sports at full-time.

"We came from a mile behind last year to win the league. A mile behind on two or three occasions as well too.

"We're still in a decent position at this minute. We've played a lot of football as well.

"I keep out the noise at the end of it all.

"I've managed this team now for about a year, give or take a month or two, and I've managed before.

"Celtic are used to winning, as you can tell by the number of trophies they've won in the last 25 years."

After returning to the club twice last season following the departures of Brendan Rodgers then Wilfried Nancy, Martin O'Neill agreed to take permanent charge in the summer after securing a league and cup double.

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd believes the current run casts doubt over his Parkhead future.

"Celtic have got a team that if they're all functioning - as we saw against Hearts - they can still cause problems to any team in the league.

"There are other managers under severe pressure. There have to be serious questions asked about Martin [O'Neill] now.

"Last season is over now... and right now, for Celtic to have lost six in the last ten in all competitions still isn't good enough. They're miles off it.

"Overall if you look at Celtic right now, where are they going?

"If you're operating as a top football club, you should already have a list of who your next managers are.

"Celtic haven't a clue what they're doing... the hierarchy will say 'we're still successful, we're still winning', but eventually it catches up with you if you don't have a plan in place."

articles.title: Bordalás: “Si el árbitro no pita, no te pares, no hay ni debate ni polémica”
articles.standfirst: El entrenador azulón compareció tras el triunfo frente al Sevilla de este domingo
articles.summary: El entrenador azulón compareció tras el triunfo frente al Sevilla de este domingo
articles.body: El Getafe venció este domingo al Sevilla en un duelo en el que la polémica del partido surgió tras el segundo gol azulón, cuando el colegiado acudió al VAR para revisar un tanto de Satriano, previo a una supuesta falta en la que el asistente levantó el banderín. Valoración: “Estamos muy contentos, veníamos a un estadio de forma espectacular, con un plantel increíble. Tenemos que mejorar algunos aspectos del juego, sobre todo las jugadas a balón parado. El equipo estaba bien y ha llegado ese gol, ha sido como una losa. Pero el equipo ha sabido reaccionar y darle la vuelta a un partido que no era sencillo. El equipo ha sabido darle la vuelta, me alegro por los chicos, esto tiene que ser un primer paso para ir mejorando y creciendo en LaLiga”. Sevilla: “Es un equipo físico y rodado que está haciendo un grandísimo trabajo. No era sencillo. El gol en contra nos ha lastrado, anímicamente nos ha hecho no tener la confianza que teníamos. En el descanso hemos hablado, éramos conscientes de la importancia del choque. Estaba muy difícil contra un gran equipo, pero supimos reaccionar. Es un resultado justo y merecido”. Reacción: “Sobre todo el de hoy, lo importante es LaLiga. Todo es importante, pero LaLiga debe ser nuestro máximo objetivo. Teníamos un déficit grande de puntos, empezábamos la jornada en puestos de descenso y era una final. El equipo ha mostrado una muy buena cara. Este es el camino, les he dicho a los jugadores que este tiene que ser el ejemplo de lo que hay que hacer en cada partido”. Jugada del 2-1: “Teníamos claro que no era falta. Se hizo justicia, teníamos muy claro en el banquillo, lo habíamos visto, pero en el monitor lo revisamos y estaba claro. El árbitro ha acertado, imperó su criterio. No tiene que haber polémica, el asistente marca una acción y el árbitro marca las decisiones”. Cómo está: “Estoy bien, siempre intento estar bien porque debo ser un ejemplo para todo el equipo, debo tener optimismo siempre. Siempre ha sido así y no va a cambiar nunca”. Vestuario: “Lo necesitaban más que yo, vienen trabajando bien y esto les va a hacer abrir los ojos para darse cuenta de lo que debemos hacer en un campo de fútbol. Me alegro por ellos, quiero dar las gracias a la afición, ha estado espectacular, saben lo importantes que son para el equipo, han llevado en volandas en momentos. Me pone los pelos de punta”. Punto de inflexión: “Sí, confiemos en que sea así, esto es un primer paso, no hemos hecho absolutamente nada. Lo que hay que conseguir es que esto sea el inicio de seguir compitiendo, mejorando aspectos de juego que debemos mejorar. A partir de ahí, entender el juego, las virtudes que tenemos”. Pararse si el asistente levanta el banderín: “Todos los técnicos les decimos a los jugadores que no se paren porque el que toma la decisión es el árbitro. Si no pita el árbitro, no tienes por qué pararte. La decisión final siempre la toma el árbitro. No hay debate ni hay polémica”.

articles.title: Diomande, el chico de los golazos
articles.standfirst: El marfileño, que lleva ya cuatro goles y cuatro asistencias, firma otra obra de arte
articles.summary: El marfileño, que lleva ya cuatro goles y cuatro asistencias, firma otra obra de arte
articles.body: Cada vez quedan menos adjetivos para calificar la irrupción de Yan Diomande. Frente al Racing, el joven extremo volvió a levantar a la grada de sus asientos con una nueva obra de arte para su colección particular... en la que lleva ya cuatro goles y cuatro asistencias desde que se soltó por completo tras un arranque dubitativo después del gran desembolso blanco en verano. Corría el minuto 36 cuando el Madrid provocó un córner. El balón voló directo al corazón del área, pero la defensa del Racing logró repeler el peligro en primera instancia. El rechace, sin embargo, cayó en la frontal del área, donde apareció Diomande libre de marca. Sin pensárselo dos veces, el marfileño enganchó un zapatazo brutal de primeras que se coló como un obús en la portería defendida por Agirrezabala. El impacto de Diomande no solo se mide en el área contraria, sino también en su sacrificio sin balón, un aspecto que no ha pasado desapercibido para las grandes leyendas del club. Una voz autorizada como Toni Kroos analizó la actualidad del equipo y la reciente ausencia de Vinícius en el Clásico, dejando un valioso consejo para el brasileño basado, precisamente, en el trabajo del nuevo ídolo de la afición. "Vini no necesita una gran técnica para hacer daño. Me hubiera gustado verle frente a Cancelo, que deja mucho espacio a sus espaldas y podía haberle hecho mucho daño", explicó. Sin embargo, Kroos fue muy claro al señalar el camino que debe seguir el extremo para recuperar su hueco indiscutible en el once titular: "Vini tiene que defender como lo hicieron Diomande y Bellingham". Un tirón de orejas con tintes de elogio para un Diomande que, además de tener el gol en las botas, se ha ganado el respeto del madridismo corriendo hacia atrás.

articles.summary: El central del Sevilla, autor del gol, no ve claro el 2-1 del Getafe
articles.body: Kike Salas, defensa del Sevilla, dijo este domingo, tras la derrota por 3-1 contra el Getafe, que el "linier levantó la bandera" en la acción de Andrés García sobre Manu Bueno en el origen del 2-1 del conjunto madrileño y opinó que "ha sido falta clara". "Estábamos preguntado al árbitro, pero a mí no me comentó nada. Veo que el linier levanta la bandera y creo que ha sido falta clara. Tampoco podemos hacer mucho. He tenido un golpe de cabeza (por un pelotazo) y estoy bastante mareado y no puedo decir más. Vamos a seguir remando hasta el final y a seguir a por todas", valoró a 'Dazn'. El Sevilla mostró dos caras diferentes entre la primera parte y la segunda. "En la primera nos estábamos encontrando bastante bien con el gol, ellos han tenido pocas ocasiones, ha llegado el gol de ellos, un gol que he visto que el linier levanta la bandera, había sido falta a Manu Bueno y no podemos entrar ahí", añadió. "El equipo ha hecho un gran esfuerzo, no hemos podido llevarnos nada de aquí, pero confianza plena en mi equipo", apuntó el defensa, que consideró que el Getafe "aprieta bastante en su campo", pero valoró que "tampoco" era un "partido descontrolado" por su parte cuando llegaron los goles del conjunto azulón.

articles.title: Cuenta atrás para el Mundial 2027: 300 días, 30 billetes y Ventanas decisivas de máxima emoción
articles.standfirst: La Copa del Mundo calienta motores: mascota, cronómetro activado y pistoletazo de salida a una recta final con Ventanas de órdago en Europa, Asia, América y África. ¿Qué se juega cada selección?
articles.summary: La Copa del Mundo calienta motores: mascota, cronómetro activado y pistoletazo de salida a una recta final con Ventanas de órdago en Europa, Asia, América y África. ¿Qué se juega cada selección?
articles.body: La cuenta atrás para el inicio de la Copa del Mundo 2027 ya ha empezado: 300 días de máxima emoción por delante hasta el próximo 27 de agosto con 30 selecciones buscando un billete en las próximas decisivas Ventanas entre noviembre y febrero para acompañar a Catar y Turquía, ya clasificadas. Para celebrar el pistoletazo de salida, y tras la reciente presentación de Suhail como la mascota oficial del campeonato, se activó el espectacular reloj Tissot, cronometrador oficial de la Copa del Mundo, en un evento por todo lo alto que recuerda a todas las selecciones que en el Camino a Catar, tras más de un año de apasionantes eliminatorias, cada victoria cuenta en Europa, América, Asia y África. La selección española conoce bien lo que significa conquistar el mundo. Campeona en 2006 y 2019, España aspira a regresar al gran escaparate internacional y afronta unas decisivas Ventanas de noviembre tras los dos reveses consecutivos de agosto ante Portugal (89-95) y Grecia (108-106 en la prórroga). España visita Montenegro (26/11) y recibe a Grecia (29/11), dos rivales directos en un Grupo I que venderá caros los tres billetes para la Copa del Mundo: Ucrania lidera el grupo con 6-2 seguida de España y Georgia con 5-3 y por detrás, Portugal, Grecia y Montenegro acumulan un 4-4. La próxima ventana puede alterar por completo ese escenario. Una doble victoria permitiría a España dar un paso de gigante hacia Catar. Dos derrotas, por el contrario, podrían situarla en una posición muy comprometida antes de la última ventana de febrero, cuando tendrá que visitar Portugal y recibir de nuevo a Montenegro. No solo importa ganar. En una competición con clasificaciones tan ajustadas, las diferencias de puntos y los posibles empates entre selecciones pueden resultar determinantes. Cada posesión, cada defensa y cada canasta pueden adquirir una importancia difícil de imaginar a estas alturas. De las 32 selecciones que iniciaron la fase europea, solo 24 siguen en la lucha por los 12 billetes mundialistas. Y una de ellas ya puede hacer planes para Catar: Turquía (8-0). Pero quedan once plazas europeas por adjudicar y nombres de enorme tradición todavía tienen trabajo por delante. En el grupo J, Serbia (6-2) e Italia (5-3) persiguen a la selección turca (8-0), con Lituania (4-4) intentando recortar distancias y meterse en la pelea por los dos billetes restantes del grupo. El Serbia-Italia del 29 de noviembre aparece como uno de los grandes duelos de la próxima ventana. El grupo K presenta otra batalla de altura. Alemania, vigente campeona del mundo, comparte un balance de 7-1 con Croacia y Polonia. Las tres selecciones parten con ventaja, aunque todavía tienen pendiente asegurar matemáticamente su presencia en el campeonato. Francia domina el grupo L con un balance de 7-1, seguida por Finlandia (5-3), mientras Eslovenia, Suecia, y Hungría, todas con 4-4, libran una intensa batalla por mantenerse en la zona de clasificación con Estonia (3-5) al final. Noviembre podrá dejar nuevos pasajeros rumbo a Doha, pero también selecciones obligadas a jugarse toda una clasificación en los últimos encuentros de febrero. Al otro lado del Atlántico, la clasificación tampoco está cerrada. Estados Unidos, Argentina, Brasil y Canadá siguen avanzando hacia Catar, aunque la competencia obliga incluso a las grandes potencias a mantener la concentración por las siete plazas (tres mejores de cada grupo y el mejor cuarto) para la Copa del Mundo. Canadá encabeza el grupo F con un pleno de ocho victorias, mientras Argentina y Uruguay presentan un balance de 6-2. Bahamas, con 4-4, trata de recortar distancias y mantener vivas sus aspiraciones. En el grupo E, Estados Unidos lidera la clasificación con siete victorias y una derrota. República Dominicana y Brasil le siguen con 6-2, mientras México, con 5-3, aspira a romper el dominio del trío de cabeza. Colombia (3-5) y Chile (2-6) tampoco han agotado sus opciones. Con este sistema de clasificación no bastará con vigilar a los rivales directos… Lo que suceda en la otra mitad del cuadro también puede resultar determinante. Las próximas citas, entre el 26 y el 30 de noviembre, serán decisivas para aclarar ese panorama. El desenlace llegará en febrero de 2027, con una última jornada especialmente diseñada para preservar la igualdad competitiva y evitar que algunos equipos jueguen conociendo resultados definitivos de sus rivales concentrándose seis partidos el 25 y otros 6 el 28. En Asia y Oceanía, la clasificación presenta una particularidad: Catar ya tiene garantizada su participación como anfitriona, por lo que quedan siete plazas adicionales por repartir entre las selecciones participantes: los tres mejores de cada grupo y el mejor cuarto. Australia ha impuesto su autoridad en el grupo E con ocho victorias en ocho encuentros. Nueva Zelanda le sigue con 6-2, mientras Irán (5-3), Jordania (5-3) y Filipinas (4-4) mantienen una interesante pugna por los puestos que permiten acceder al Mundial. El grupo F ofrece una lucha igualmente atractiva. Japón y Líbano comparten la cabeza con seis victorias y dos derrotas, seguidos de China, que acumula un 5-3, y Corea del Sur, con 4-4. Arabia Saudí (3-5) también sigue en la carrera, mientras Catar (4-4) continúa compitiendo pese a tener su clasificación asegurada. La ventana de noviembre, del 26 al 29, incluye enfrentamientos tan atractivos como Líbano-Japón, Irán-Australia o Arabia Saudí-China. Partidos que pueden perfilar la distribución de las plazas antes de que febrero dicte sentencia. A diferencia de las otras tres regiones, África no disputará partidos clasificatorios en noviembre. Su competición, organizada mediante concentraciones en lugar del formato habitual de ida y vuelta, ya ha completado cuatro de sus cinco ventanas. Las doce selecciones supervivientes afrontarán su último asalto entre el 25 y el 28 de febrero de 2027, con cinco plazas mundialistas en juego. Camerún y Sudán del Sur lideran el grupo E con siete victorias y dos derrotas, perseguidos por Guinea, con seis triunfos. Túnez y Nigeria también conservan opciones con 5-4, mientras Cabo Verde busca prolongar su sueño mundialista (3-6). En el grupo F, Senegal y Costa de Marfil encabezan la clasificación con idéntico balance de 7-2. Angola y Mali les siguen con 6-3, mientras Egipto (4-5) y la República Democrática del Congo (3-6) intentarán alterar el orden establecido en la última ventana. Los dos primeros de cada grupo y el mejor tercero obtendrán el billete. Una fórmula que promete emoción hasta el último encuentro, especialmente en una región donde las distancias entre las principales selecciones se han reducido considerablemente. Mientras las selecciones se juegan su futuro sobre el parqué, Doha avanza en los preparativos de una Copa del Mundo que se disputará del 27 de agosto al 12 de septiembre de 2027. La organización ha presentado recientemente a Suhail, la mascota oficial del campeonato. Inspirada en Canopus, una estrella conocida en la tradición árabe por servir de referencia a navegantes y viajeros, Suhail simboliza ese espíritu de descubrimiento y conexión entre culturas. Su apariencia dorada y su camiseta con el número 27 remiten directamente al país anfitrión y al año del torneo. También está ya en marcha el reloj oficial de Tissot, presentado en el corazón de Doha como una de las grandes señas visuales de la cuenta atrás. Su diseño combina la silueta de un aro gigante con elementos propios de la relojería, en un guiño al vínculo entre el deporte y el tiempo.

articles.title: Man Utd: Gary Neville says club are in a rut and is unimpressed with Lisandro Martinez amid tough run of games for Michael Carrick's side
articles.summary: Gary Neville on Manchester United's plight: "It feels like the club is stuck in a rut. It's stuck in a rut in terms of results, it's now nine without a win, which is obviously a really horrible run to be in at any point. It's a real depression of results, a depression of performances."
articles.body:
Saturday's 2-0 defeat at Chelsea extended United's winless run to nine games in all competitions - their longest since 1984 - and puts them at risk of falling into the relegation zone before the next international break.

Head coach Michael Carrick said after the loss at Chelsea that he expects to remain in charge for Tuesday night's Champions League visit of Roma.

Describing United's current predicament, Neville said: "It's very difficult. It feels like the club is stuck in a rut. It's stuck in a rut in terms of results, it's now nine without a win, which is obviously a really horrible run to be in at any point.

"People will talk about the first half (against Chelsea) and say that there were some good things, and there were. But when things aren't going your way, you've got to be able to dig in.

"You've got to keep your discipline and you've got be able to get through points in a game when your opponents are doing quite well - and Manchester United can't do that right now.

"As soon as they go a goal down they fall to pieces.

"I don't think it's at that stage (where Manchester United are in a relegation battle). I don't think they will end up there, but it's a worry. It's a real depression of results, a depression of performances.

"And they've got difficult games coming up.

"Any team that is organised, that's got a combination or two about them, will cause Manchester United problems.

"Roma could do that on Tuesday, Aston Villa next weekend are very organised, [they] know how to play. After that, they come to Anfield.

"There are a lot of big games in front for Manchester United in these next few weeks, but it's really worrying."

Nev: If I played like Martinez, I'd be curled up in a ball

Neville explained he is distinctly unimpressed by Lisandro Martinez's performances. Martinez was sent off in the loss at Stamford Bridge on just his second start since his extraordinary criticism of the club's hierarchy .

"Lisandro Martinez? That's what I expect from him, to be honest with you," Neville said.

"I said the other week - and you've got to respect hat he is a World Cup winner - but every time I watch him for Manchester United he is at fault for a goal.

"He was at fault for two yesterday. The first goal is solely on him.

If I was giving away the goals that he is giving away, I wouldn't be doing interviews. And to be fair, I wouldn't be speaking out, because I have to say, I would be curled up in a ball, playing like that for Manchester United.

"We all give goals away as defenders, but the quantity of goals he gives away is remarkable. And that defence is nowhere near good enough and it falls apart every time it is put under big pressure."

articles.title: Hearts 1-2 Hibernian: Jamie McGrath scores winner as Hibs beat rivals at Hampden for first time to set up Scottish League Cup final vs Rangers
articles.summary: Report as Hibs beat Hearts at Hampden Park for the first time in their history; Jamie McGrath got the winner as the Leith side came from behind to win 2-1 and set up a clash with Rangers in the final on December 13
articles.body:
A frenetic derby got up and running in the fourth minute when Jambos attacker Claudio Braga headed in from a corner but returning Hibs striker Martin Boyle deservedly levelled in the 19th minute with a poacher's goal.

A compelling encounter continued and midfielder Jamie McGrath put the on-top Hibees ahead three minutes before the interval, which gave the Gorgie side time to reset and put pressure on their opponents after the break.

Although Hearts retained a threat, a stout defensive display by the Leith team means they will meet Rangers in the final at the national stadium on December 13.

Hearts had won the four previous meetings between the teams at Hampden - in 2006, 2012, 2020 and 2022 - but this was Hibs' day.

articles.title: Kirby Smart Calls Out Players' 'Hunger' in NIL Era in Viral Video After Georgia's Win vs. Florida
articles.summary: Georgia head coach Kirby Smart explained how he believes the NIL era has impacted the drive of college football players after the No. 3 Bulldogs secured a 27-8 win over No. 17 Florida on Saturday.
articles.body:
Georgia head coach Kirby Smart explained how he believes the NIL era has impacted the drive of college football players after the No. 3 Bulldogs secured a 27-8 win over No. 17 Florida on Saturday.

"It does seem different," Smart told reporters when asked about the current state of the SEC compared to the last 25 years. "I've asked several coaches about it and we all have speculation. I don't want to get judgement on what it is. Everybody's practicing less, but everybody's getting injured more and it doesn't make sense. It doesn't add up because we're not at the point of the ninth game yet. Nobody's played any more than they normally would have right now."

"I don't know that the players are any different," he added. "I think about the teams we had in 2021 and 2022, how physical they were and how they practiced. We can't even get close to that now. Is it different culture that guys don't want to as much? I don't know. They were definitely hungrier, because there was a motivation to make it. A lot of these guys, they make more than I was made until I was 40. So, it's just a different day and age."

While Georgia sits atop the SEC standings, every team in the conference has suffered at least one loss this season.

Parity has been more prevalent compared to past years, as 14 of the SEC's 16 teams have lost at least two games to conference opponents to begin the season.

Health issues have also surfaced among key players across the college football landscape, although they haven't been limited to the SEC.

Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor was ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season after undergoing toe surgery , while Ohio State passer Julian Sayin is in danger of missing the rest of the year due to an injury to his right throwing arm.

Oregon signal-caller Dante Moore will also be sidelined through the end of his 2026 campaign with a concussion .

Smart appears to believe that the NIL deals given out to players have decreased their intensity in practice compared to the era before NIL, which may be affecting their preparation for the physicality of regular-season games.

According to Stewart Mandel, David Ubben and Sam Khan Jr. of The Athletic, SEC teams have an average NIL budget of $33 million to $38 million. It represents the highest mark among all conferences.

As for Smart, his team will look to continue building momentum during an upcoming matchup with No. 12 Ole Miss on Saturday.

articles.title: Michael Carrick's Man Utd support explained as fans believe reason for worst start in 40 years goes beyond dugout
articles.summary: Why haven't Manchester United fans turned on Michael Carrick even though it looks like he's living on borrowed time?
articles.body:
When things get this bad, managers can be forgiven for heading straight down the tunnel after another defeat - especially if their side have made their worst start to a season in 40 years.

Michael Carrick did not have to think twice before heading towards the United supporters after the final whistle at Stamford Bridge following Saturday's 2-0 defeat .

Those fans had not seen their team win for almost two months, but they showed warmth, appreciation and respect for the manager who has overseen a run of nine league games without a win.

No matter how much worse things get, it is difficult to imagine hardcore United fans turning on their manager.

No team has won fewer Premier League games than United this season. Only goal difference is keeping Carrick's side out of the relegation zone .

Make no mistake, on their current trajectory of 0.77 points per game, United are heading for relegation for the first time since 1974. They would end the season with fewer than 30 points, which would almost certainly mean Championship football next season.

Things have got so bad some United fans think relegation would be a blessing in disguise if it forces their owners to sell the club.

So, despite all the doom and gloom, and the damning statistics, why have United fans not turned on their manager?

Carrick is a class act and he still embodies the values United are meant to represent as a club.

Carrick played under Sir Alex Ferguson and is an old-school manager in the sense that he wants to keep everything inside the dressing room. Some fans may want him to rant and rave and show more emotion in public but you are never going to get that from Carrick.

When it comes to the media, United are like Real Madrid and Barcelona. Everything that happens at the club is headline news - especially in the social media age. United fans feel like they are under siege.

Carrick is on their side. He gives very little away when he speaks in public. He wears his club suit with pride and always says what is in the best interests of the club. He never makes it about himself. The clue is in the name: United.

Changing the manager is not going to fix the long-term problems at the club . United fans know that and that is why they are not going to hound Carrick out and watch him being replaced by another manager who has to operate in the same structure.

United have had seven permanent managers since Ferguson retired in 2013 and, despite varying levels of relative success in cup competitions, none of them has been able to mount a genuine title challenge.

A long list of former United players have now joined fans in arguing that things are not going to get better at United until the club has new owners.

The media are sometimes criticised for not highlighting issues with United's ownership structure but anyone who has time on their hands can go and check old newspapers from 2005.

The vast majority of football reporters and commentators who covered the Glazer family's takeover warned that leveraged buyouts - the acquisition of a company using a high proportion of borrowed money (debt) - should not be allowed in football. Leveraged buyouts of the kind the Glazers used to buy United are no longer allowed in English football. That is no consolation for United fans.

United fans don't traditionally turn on their managers

It seems almost inevitable that Carrick will lose his job and his body language sometimes resembles a man who is resigned to his fate.

If Carrick does go this month, he can walk out of Old Trafford with his head held high - and come back whenever he wants.

United fans are proud of the fact that they have historically not turned on their managers. Fans have become disaffected and disillusioned with the managers who have followed in Ferguson's footsteps but there have been no mutinies.

United supporters of a certain age still remember the lone fan who turned up to Old Trafford with a banner in December 1989 declaring that Ferguson should leave after "three years of excuses".

Ferguson did not say goodbye and the rest is history - including 13 league titles and two European Cups.

Fans don't trust chiefs to make the right calls

When Jim Ratcliffe bought a minority stake in United in 2024, the Glazers agreed to let him take control of football operations.

Erik ten Hag was the manager at the time and despite initial misgivings he was given a contract extension after winning the 2024 FA Cup final. He was sacked and replaced by Ruben Amorim just five months later. Amorim lasted 14 months before he was sacked after he criticised the way the club was being run in a press conference.

Carrick took over in an interim capacity in January and he was given the full-time job in the summer after he led United back into the Champions League with a third-place finish in the Premier League.

The key decision makers below Ratcliffe are chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, who both used to work at Manchester City.

Highly-respected sporting director Dan Ashworth left in December 2024 after just five months - after spending five months on gardening leave at Newcastle United.

United's top targets to replace Carrick are former Newcastle and Bournemouth manager Eddie Howe and former Germany and Bayern Munich manager Julian Nagelsmann.

Both of them are strong candidates but United fans do not seem to be that excited by the prospect of either of them taking over.

A clean slate and a fresh start may mean they would be able to get more out of this group of players than Carrick but there are no guarantees in football.

If Unai Emery was available, he would be the favourite to take over but he is doing a great job at Aston Villa and is under contract until 2029.

In any case, swapping Villa for United at this stage of his career would mean dropping down 19 places in the Champions League table and eight places in the Premier League.

Clubs in the Premier League are also duty-bound to act in utmost good faith towards each other, which makes any move for Emery fraught with complications.

articles.title: Braulio Vázquez, director deportivo del Valencia: "Que nadie piense que el mercado de invierno va a arreglar esto"
articles.standfirst: El director deportivo del Valencia describe su toma de contacto con los nuevos inversores: "Quieren información"
articles.summary: El director deportivo del Valencia describe su toma de contacto con los nuevos inversores: "Quieren información"
articles.body: Braulio Vázquez no mira al mercado para salir del pozo. El director deportivo del Valencia, recién incorporado a la estructura deportiva del club en plena transición accionarial y deportiva, lanzó un mensaje de realismo antes del encuentro frente al Elche. Con el equipo en puestos de descenso y sumido en una crisis de resultados que amenaza con complicar seriamente la temporada, el gallego descartó que todo el esfuerzo haya que ponerlo en los posibles refuerzos de enero. "Que nadie piense que el mercado de invierno va a arreglar esto", advirtió en los micrófonos de Movistar, poniendo el foco en la necesidad inmediata de que la plantilla reaccione sobre el terreno de juego. Vázquez reconoció que el contexto que se encontró al aterrizar en Mestalla era tan complejo como esperaba. "Sabía dónde venía y que el Valencia es un club enorme", señaló, aunque insistió en que la prioridad absoluta pasa por abandonar una situación clasificatoria que mantiene al conjunto valencianista en la zona roja. "Lo importante es ahora empezar a ganar", remarcó. El director deportivo también se refirió a los primeros contactos con los nuevos inversores de Pitchwise que han desembarcado en el accionariado valencianista junto a Kiat Lim. Según explicó, tanto él como los nuevos responsables se encuentran todavía en una fase de análisis y recopilación de información para conocer en profundidad la situación de la entidad. "No he hablado tanto con ellos. He hablado con Corey [Woolfolk] y con el presi. Ellos acaban de llegar y yo llevo un mes. Todos estamos intentando tener más información sobre el club y yo también", afirmó. En clave deportiva, Vázquez pidió prudencia respecto al futuro de Kayne Van Oevelen. El portero neerlandés, lesionado actualmente, había sido señalado en las últimas semanas por una posible interrupción de su cesión desde el Ipswich Town. Sin embargo, el director deportivo evitó anticipar decisiones. "Está lesionado y fastidiado. Queremos correr antes que andar. Faltan dos meses de competición y no sabemos lo que va a pasar", explicó. Como ejemplo de los cambios que pueden producirse durante una temporada recordó el caso de Stole Dimitrievski: "Parecía que iba a salir por la titularidad de Agirrezabala [ahora en el Racing] y acabó siendo titular".

articles.title: Pablo Fornals recupera el corazón del malaguismo
articles.standfirst: El canterano marcó pero no lo celebró en La Cartuja
articles.summary: El canterano marcó pero no lo celebró en La Cartuja
articles.body: Hay historias que nunca terminan de romperse del todo. La de Pablo Fornals y el Málaga CF es una de ellas. El fútbol volvió a cruzar sus caminos en La Cartuja, aunque esta vez con un desenlace muy diferente al de aquella primera etapa en la que el centrocampista terminó convirtiéndose en uno de los grandes talentos surgidos de La Academia. Fornals se formó en el Málaga y llegó al primer equipo con apenas 18 años. Durante dos temporadas disputó 59 encuentros y marcó siete goles, antes de dar el salto al Villarreal previo pago de una cláusula cercana a los 12 millones de euros. Una operación que generó un profundo malestar entre parte de la afición malaguista, especialmente porque el conjunto amarillo ya había acudido anteriormente al mercado de La Academia para hacerse con jugadores como los Samus y Ontiveros. Aquella salida dejó una herida que tardó en cicatrizar. El propio Fornals explicó años después que el regreso a La Rosaleda con el Villarreal fue uno de los episodios más difíciles de su carrera. En una entrevista en el podcast Offsiders reconoció haber recibido insultos y explicó lo doloroso que había sido regresar al estadio donde se había formado: "No lo he pasado tan mal en un estadio o me ha dolido tanto volver a La Rosaleda y que me insultaran. Pero volvería las veces que hicieran falta. No les guardo ningún tipo de rencor porque yo sé perfectamente qué fue lo que pasó". Fornals fue uno de los futbolistas más destacados del Betis y, justo antes del descanso, apareció para marcar el 2-0. El castellonense aprovechó una segunda jugada tras un saque de esquina, controló en la frontal y definió con tranquilidad para poner tierra de por medio en el marcador. Pero hubo un detalle que no pasó desapercibido: Fornals no celebró el gol. En lugar de festejarlo con sus compañeros, levantó las manos y pidió perdón a la afición del Málaga. Un gesto sencillo, pero cargado de significado. El futbolista que durante años fue señalado por una parte del malaguismo mostró respeto hacia el club que le abrió las puertas del fútbol profesional. Quizá no borra todo lo ocurrido, pero sí sirve para cerrar una historia que llevaba demasiado tiempo pendiente de un último capítulo. El fútbol, a veces, también ofrece la oportunidad de hacer las paces.
